title: Check yourself: The Agent SDK: tools, permissions, hooks and custom tools

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A developer lists Read and Grep in allowed_tools, and expects shell commands to be out of reach. What happens?

options.text: Bash is removed from the agent's context before the first turn
options.says: Ruled out because only a bare name in disallowed_tools "removes the tool from Claude's context altogether", and allowed_tools is not that setting.

options.text: Bash remains available, and its calls fall through to the mode
options.says: The page says allowed_tools "does not restrict Claude to only these tools", and that unlisted tools "fall through to permission_mode and can_use_tool".

options.text: Bash calls are denied in every permission mode
options.says: Ruled out because allowed_tools "auto-approves the tools you list", so it approves and does not deny.

options.text: Bash calls are approved automatically with no prompt
options.says: Ruled out because "Tools not listed are still available, and calls to them that need approval fall through to the permission mode and canUseTool."

questions.stem: A PreToolUse hook returns deny for a call that a matching allow rule would approve, in acceptEdits mode. What happens to the call?

options.text: It runs, and the allow rule wins
options.says: Ruled out because "hooks run before every other step, and a hook deny applies even in bypassPermissions mode", so an allow rule cannot override it.

options.text: It goes to the callback, which decides
options.says: Ruled out because "The callback sees only what nothing earlier decided.", and the hook has decided.

options.text: It waits for the permission mode to decide
options.says: Ruled out because the mode is checked after the hooks, and "Hooks run first, so a hook can deny a call outright".

options.text: It is blocked, and no later step is consulted
options.says: The page says "Hooks run first, so a hook can deny a call outright", and "Each step can end the decision."

questions.stem: A custom in-process tool divides by zero and the handler throws without catching. What does Claude see?

options.text: Nothing, because the query aborts before any result is produced
options.says: Ruled out because "A handler error doesn't stop the agent loop."

options.text: The raw exception message as an error result, and the loop continues
options.says: The page says the in-process server catches an uncaught exception and returns it as an error result that carries the raw exception message, and the loop goes on.

options.text: A message that you compose, since uncaught errors are reported as written
options.says: Ruled out because "Claude sees the message you compose" only when the handler catches the error and returns is_error, and an uncaught exception does not do that.

options.text: A generic failure notice with the message stripped for safety
options.says: Ruled out because the result is an error result "that carries the raw exception message", not a stripped one.
